title: Find why Vercel builds hit out_of_memory at random when the Next processes peak near 2.7 GB

source.ref: Production deploy of 7426903a (#4805) ended ERROR out_of_memory on 2026-11-10 15:28Z; earlier main deploy 7d71b670 did the same.

detail:
MEASURED 2026-11-10, not assumed. Of the last 30 Vercel deployments, 5 ended ERROR with out_of_memory (1 production, 4 previews). Every one died the same way: compile finished (about 93 s), then the build was killed at 'Collecting page data using 3 workers', and Vercel printed '.next/routes-manifest.json couldn't be found'. The same trees build fine on neighbouring pushes: a main deploy of the previous commit (#4806, 781c67b) and of the next ones were READY, and the HYG-215 branch OOM'd at ab52647 then built at 4896bc6. check-build-memory reads a healthy main build (2366d904) at a peak of 2770 MB summed across 4 next processes against a 7168 MB budget, so the Next processes are not near the limit. That rules out the fan-out creep the standing rule expects and points at something the sampler does not see (other processes in the container, page-data workers on a cold start, a smaller machine) or at platform noise. The failing build never prints a reading, because the sampler is killed with it. Next steps, cheapest first: (1) have the sampler write its running peak to the build log every 30 s so a killed build still leaves a number; (2) compare the Build system report (Input source code 1902 MB, node_modules 1004 MB, .git pack 337 MB) across a failing and a passing build; (3) only if the peak is real, try experimental.cpus = 2 on one preview and read the sampler. Do not raise the budget and do not cut routes until a reading says which. Production keeps serving the last READY deploy when a build fails, so this costs deploy freshness, not uptime.

Packet E observability slice: the detached sampler publishes the first observed peak and then a running peak every 30 seconds to the build log. Postbuild uses the same reading and unchanged 7168 MB budget. The investigation stays open pending the manual Vercel evidence.

CLOSED 2026-11-16. Cause found and the 20-READY test met. Read from the build logs of the last three READY production builds (f47efefc, 11595588, 0f0623a7; 4 cores, 8 GB Standard machine, cold compile): container peak 7784, 7859 and 7768 MB, landing at the end of 'Creating an optimized production build'. The process that grows is next-build, the Turbopack compile, at 5886 to 6494 MB RSS in the last 10 s sample before the peak; every other process totals under 500 MB, and after compile the container falls to 3000 to 3600 MB. The earlier random kills were this peak crossing 8192 MB on some builds (7937 MB was killed on 2026-11-15). The postbuild budget never saw it because it sums processes named next, which read about 100 MB during compile. Since HYG-240 (MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0, #5013) there are 38 READY deploys in a row and no out_of_memory. Margin is still only 333 to 424 MB, so shrinking the compile and gating the container reading move to HYG-241.

verify.evidence: MET 2026-11-16 on both tests. Vercel deployments list: 38 READY in a row (11 production, 27 preview) from the HYG-240 deploy (5dc03bfd, 2026-11-15 22:08Z) to 2026-11-16 14:40Z, no ERROR and no out_of_memory; the 33 CANCELED in that span are 32 ignored-build-step skips and one superseded main build. The HYG-224 sampler names the process: next-build (the Turbopack compile) at 5.9 to 6.5 GB in the last sample before the container peak. Re-open if any deploy ends out_of_memory; the thin margin is tracked on HYG-241.
